scope: Bounded semantic replay convergence for dedicated signed PIX settlement

criteria.description: The persisted provider receipt already contains claims_fingerprint, but the worker/B1 path keys semantic idempotency only by provider event ID; distinct equivalent events can therefore reach a terminal attempt conflict after the first settlement.
criteria.limitations: This is source-level selection evidence; the intentional PostgreSQL RED is still required.

criteria.description: The smallest safe boundary is the dedicated worker-to-B1 settlement seam: transport the stored claims fingerprint, converge only after the billing lock, and mark only the duplicate delivery applied with a sanitized canonical-replay code.
criteria.limitations: No schema change is expected; if implementation evidence proves otherwise, authority must be revalidated before expanding scope.

criteria.description: A disposable PostgreSQL test can create two authenticated receipts with distinct event IDs and equal claims, process them sequentially/concurrently, and assert one financial effect, two applied deliveries and no cross-tenant leakage.
criteria.limitations: Fresh RED/GREEN, regression, quality, independent review attempt and bounded reconciliation remain pending.

gaps: The distinct-event semantic replay RED, implementation, concurrency proof, full regression, quality and independent review are not complete at gate creation.
conditions: Preserve the dedicated signed protocol, append-only receipts, B1 single-writer financial effects and explicit global IN_PROGRESS/PARTIAL with promotion BLOCKED.
Do not turn claims equivalence into a cross-tenant or provider identity shortcut; all account/attempt/billing/transaction claims remain authoritative.

authority.actor: Ricardo (repository owner), via fresh local residual scouting after unavailable auxiliary scouts
authority.decision: Authorize reversible repository implementation, focused module/worker tests and disposable PostgreSQL proof for equivalent distinct-event convergence. Exclude provider, credentials, target, production, deployment, schema expansion unless proven necessary, release and global ERP promotion.
authority.expires_or_revalidates: Revalidate before changing the signed protocol, the legacy consumer, provider identity, financial schema, target/production behavior or global readiness.

revalidation_triggers: Changes to pix_provider_events.claims_fingerprint or the 0111 ingress contract
Changes to the shared B1 confirmed PIX settlement primitive
Changes to encounter_non_cash_receipts uniqueness or settlement proof semantics
Any provider, target, production, deployment or release operation
next_action: Write and run the intentional RED with two distinct event IDs and equal claims before changing implementation.
